service.name: Wedding music in Colorado
service.serviceType: Live music for wedding ceremonies, cocktail hours and receptions
service.description: Acoustic and Spanish guitar for the ceremony, a jazz or acoustic duo for the cocktail hour, and a DJ for the reception, booked on one contract across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What parts of a wedding day need music?
faqs.a: Three, and they are three different jobs. The ceremony needs a prelude, a processional and a recessional. The cocktail hour needs something guests can talk across. The reception needs a floor that fills. One booking can carry all three, and most couples book two of them live and the third as a DJ.

faqs.q: Can one booking cover the ceremony and the cocktail hour?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the most common shape here. The same players walk from the ceremony space to wherever cocktails are happening, on one contract, one load-in and one invoice. That also solves the gap while the couple is away for photographs, because nothing has to be set up in between.

faqs.q: Do we need a band for the whole wedding?
faqs.a: No, and most Colorado weddings are better served without one. Live players carry the ceremony and the cocktail hour, where volume and attention have to be handled by a person reading the crowd. A DJ carries the reception, where a floor has to stay full for hours.

faqs.q: How far ahead should wedding music be booked?
faqs.a: Wedding dates get decided ten to twelve months out, and twelve to eighteen for a mountain venue or a fall Saturday. Music is usually shopped nine to fourteen months out, which is later than the venue and earlier than almost everything else on the list.

faqs.q: Do you play outdoor weddings in Colorado?
faqs.a: Yes, and most of them are outdoors. Outdoors adds three requirements at any size: a covered, level and dry performance area, power run to it, and a move-indoors call written before the day. Colorado evenings drop fast after sunset, and instruments and electronics both stop behaving in the cold.
